_comment: Guide-matching configuration. Controls how detected technology terms map to PDF guide filenames. Edit this file to add new mappings without touching Python code.

reference_guides._comment: Guides that are reference-only (e.g. alarms index). They match almost every term because they cover every topic superficially. Excluded from scoring and auto-selection, but users can still manually check them in the UI.

install_upgrade_terms._comment: Terms that trigger auto-selection of install/upgrade guides. When any of these terms are detected in bug/RCA content, guides matching 'install_guide_patterns' filenames are auto-checked.

sdwan._comment: Concept-to-guide mapping. When a term (key) is detected in bug/RCA content, guides whose filenames contain ANY of the listed patterns (values) are auto-checked. Use this for terms that don't literally appear in guide filenames but semantically belong to a specific guide. Patterns are matched as substrings against the normalized filename (lowercase, no .pdf). Built from actual book table-of-contents analysis.
sdwan._comment_routing: ── Routing concepts (cross-product: routing-book-xe, b-routing-cg-*, b-bgp-*, b-multicast-*, etc.) ──
sdwan._comment_xproduct: ── Cross-product concepts (match dedicated books on IOS-XR platforms) ──
sdwan._comment_scoured: ── Auto-discovered concepts from book TOC analysis (scour_books.py) ──

ASR9000._comment_scoured: ── Auto-discovered concepts from book TOC analysis (scour_books.py) ──

product_noise._comment: Product-specific terms to SKIP during guide matching. These terms appear in most/all filenames for a product and would match every guide. Keys are product folder codes.

filename_noise_words._comment: Common words that appear in guide filenames. Any detected term that is a substring of these words gets skipped to avoid false matches (e.g. 'gui' inside 'guide').

stop_words._comment: English stop words stripped from terms before filename matching. Filenames often drop these (e.g. 'monitor and maintain' becomes 'monitor-maintain' in the filename).
